title: Adjustments 2: hedging a trade you hold
summary: When to add a protective buy to a trade you already hold, how to do it in the builder, and when closing is the better choice.

questions.q: Which is a good reason to hedge a trade you already hold?
options: Results were announced for before your expiry
questions.why: A new event before expiry is the classic reason to add protection.

questions.q: You sold the 900 put. Which buy hedges it?
options: Two 850 puts for every one sold
questions.why: Same type, further out of the money, no more lots than sold.

questions.q: The hedge would cost most of the premium still left in your sold leg. Usually better:
questions.why: When protection eats the remaining reward, closing is simpler and frees the margin.

questions.q: Your stop has already been hit. Should you hedge instead of exiting?
options: Yes, to avoid booking the loss
questions.why: Hedging after the stop is a way of not taking the loss; the rule is to exit.

questions.q: Before Level 6, can you add a protective buy to a sold leg you already hold?
options: Yes, if it protects that sold leg: same type, further out, no more lots
questions.why: The buy rule checks the order against your open position, so a protective buy is allowed.
